messages:
ivy: heads-up — after the 09:30 canary we saw a 12-18% tail latency regression for small requests (<64 tokens) on host ingress. spike shows in p50->p99. attaching quick numbers from canary vs baseline.

sam: ugh, thanks. that aligns with the mini-burst alerts i saw. any idea what changed in the deploy?

ivy: rolled kernel-selector tweak + small change to batching hinting. selector now prefers f16-kernel when model is quantized and seq_len < 64. batching hint: lower threshold for miniburst coalescing.

rachel: grabbing profiles now. preliminary flame: host parse + tokenizer CPU up ~35% on hot path. KV cache hit rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.62 on canary shard A. looks like more cache churn.

kai: also seeing increased small write syscall count on the HTTP/gRPC side. lots of 64-256b writes — gRPC framing + our chunking is emitting many small packets.

ivy: here's the kernel selector snippet we changed (simplified):
```
if is_quantized(model) and seq_len < 64:
  prefer_kernel = "f16_fast"
else:
  prefer_kernel = "fp32_stable"
```
That was meant to cut decode cycles for short sequences but maybe f16 path hits a slow export path on our runtime.

sam: can you dump pprof + the trace for a sample request? also which canary %?

deploy-bot: canary rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% (09:35)

ivy: attaching snippets (p95/p99 numbers) — baseline p99 210ms, canary p99 245ms. pprof: top is parse->tokenize->http_writev. trace shows repeated kv-lookup misses interleaved with kernel selection branch.

rachel: KV logs: eviction spikes at t=09:32 across multiple shards, concurrent loads for identical prefixes. looks like selector change altered the sequence length distribution hitting the cache keys (different prefixing).

kai: hypothesis: kernel switch caused slight TTL or key normalization mismatch? or minibatching change created more distinct keys (batch id included) so cache miss rate jumps. also writev small-writes cut TCP Nagle benefits.

sam: short-term rollback to previous kernel-selector flag until we triage?

ivy: +1. i'll flip the feature gate for selector and bump canary down to 0 while we investigate.

rachel: i'll try bumping kv cache retention and reduce shard eviction aggressiveness on canary shard to see hit-rate effects.

kai: i'll prototype an ingress coalescer that merges up to 8 small frames before parse — should reduce syscall/writev count. quick pseudo:
```
while len(buffered) < 8 and time_since_first < 2ms:
  collect_next()
coalesce_and_parse(buffered)
```
That should be safe and low-latency for short bursts.

sam: can we also add a quick metric to kernel-selector: count(kernel_taken, seq_len_bucket) so we can correlate kernel choice -> kv hit pattern?

ivy: good call. i'll add that metric and re-run a controlled synthetic canary with traffic similar to prod short-req mix.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated (selector-feature=false) by ivy at 09:48. canary scaled to 0% -> safe.

rachel: after rollback, preliminary numbers look back to baseline p99 212ms, kv hit ~0.85. writev still high but not enough to push tail above baseline.

kai: still think we should land coalescer (opt-in) and a small change to batching-hinting: only apply miniburst coalesce when measured QPS > X for that route. reduces key-variance.

sam: action items:
- ivy: add kernel-selector metrics + re-run controlled canary (owner: ivy)
- rachel: try relaxed kv-eviction on a test shard and run A/B (owner: rachel)
- kai: prototype ingress coalescer and perf diff (owner: kai)
- sam: coordinate canary once metrics available (owner: sam)

ivy: thanks. i pushed the temp rollback. we'll reconvene after the synthetic canary and the kv A/B runs.

rachel: i'll post flame graphs + raw kv stats in this thread when ready.

kai: will try a minimal coalescer patch in a branch and publish perf numbers within a day.

sam: nice triage — very actionable. :thumbsup:

ivy: closing loop for now. will ping when metrics from selector-metrics land.
